description:
io/crlf.t is 16408/16421 (docs/perl-suite-run.tsv): the 13 failing rows split into (a) :crlf layer semantics — open ">:crlf"/"<:crlf" (file and in-memory scalar-ref), write 
→
, read 
→
, tell/seek in RAW byte offsets through the translation, binmode(FH) REMOVING the layer, repeated binmode(FH,":crlf") not accumulating; and (b) PerlIO::get_layers(FH) returning the layer-name list — the test greps it for "utf8" after binmode($fh,":utf8") and checks binmode(FH) removes :utf8. cl/pcl-runtime.lisp %p-binmode-impl documents the standing decision: "PCL builds on SBCL streams and does not model PerlIO layers" (binmode is a no-op on open handles). Implementing these rows means introducing a minimal per-handle layer-stack record (name list + crlf translation wrapper + utf8 flag) — a design decision to discuss (CLAUDE.md #4), not a drive-by fix. Until then the file stays DIFF (near-green). The undef-fn crash rows (t16419-21) are get_layers; the early rows (t1-6) and t16408-16415 are :crlf translation itself.

RE-PROBED s406 (task #348 landing), and the layer is a NO-OP in BOTH directions:
    open $fh, '>:crlf'; print $fh "a
b
"   perl: 61 0d 0a 62 0d 0a   PCL: 61 0a 62 0a
    open $in, '<:crlf' over "a
b
"    perl: 610a|620a          PCL: 610d0a|620d0a
SECOND FILE FOUND, and #348 took it away again: io/crlf_through.t (`$main::use_crlf = 1; do './io/through.t'`) was 726/216 DIFF because through.t pipes its data through a which_perl child — a REAL perl child, so the 216 rows were PCL's :crlf disagreeing with perl's.  Since #348 the child is PCL, both ends share the gap, and the file reads OK 942/0.  That is PCL-vs-PCL agreement, not conformance: io/crlf.t (16408/16421, 13 rows) is now the only file measuring this.  Attribution measurement: PCL_FRESH_PERL=real reproduces 726/216 exactly.
subject: io/crlf.t: :crlf PerlIO layer + PerlIO::get_layers introspection (needs a layer model decision)
